Stage 3 · Grammar

Grammar

I'm / you're / he is / they are (+/–)
PersonPositive (+)Negative (–)
II'm from Japan.I'm not from Spain.
youYou're from the UK.You aren't from China.
he/sheShe's from Brazil.He isn't from Russia.
we/theyThey're from Turkey.We aren't from the USA.
  • am → I. is → he / she / it. are → you / we / they.
  • Negative: add not. I'm not · he isn't (is not) · they aren't (are not).
  • Countries need no “the”: I'm from Japan. But: the UK, the USA.
  • Ask: Where are you from? — Answer: I'm from…

→ more Wh- questions (why, when, how) come in Lesson 15.

🔧 Build it yourself
  • 🔧 Build it yourself
  • Build it: I am from Spain → I am NOT from Spain → I'm not from Spain.
  • ⚠ Not goes AFTER am/is/are: She is not from Rome — never 'She not from Rome' (она не из Рима).

Stage 6 · Speaking

Your turn

Write two short lines: where you're from and your nationality.

When you finish, open the model answer and check yourself.

Model answer

I'm from Spain. I'm Spanish. Nice to meet you!

Check yourself:

  • Did you use I'm from …?
  • Did you write your nationality (…-ish / -ian / -ese)?
  • Is to be correct? (I'm, he's, they're)
Talk to Sam. Answer with the words from this lesson.

Read each message. Tap 🔊 to hear Sam.

Sam

Hi! I'm Sam. 👋

Sam

Where are you from?

Sam

Cool! 🌍

Sam

I'm from the UK. I'm British.

Sam

My friend Leo… listen: I say “He are from Brazil.” 🤔

Why

he / she / it → is, not are. He is (He's) from Brazil.

Sam

Yes! “He's from Brazil.” Great catch. 🌟

Feedback

Well done: you said where you're from and fixed the verb. Next time, say your nationality out loud too.
